name: Cold desert
notes: Sparse grey chenopod shrubs (saltbush, saxaul, winterfat) and scattered bunchgrasses with cold winters; Gobi and Central Asian deserts, Great Basin/Colorado Plateau lowlands, Patagonian monte.

shrub.name: Blackbrush
shrub.source: Coleogyne ramosissima, Mojave-Great Basin transition, dark twiggy shrub 0.3-1.5 m — USDA PLANTS

traits.native_range: Coleogyne ramosissima, Mojave-Great Basin transition, dark twiggy shrub 0
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings usually come up in clumps from forgotten rodent seed caches: tiny epigeal seedlings with two oval cotyledons and small narrow opposite leaves; most die at the cotyledon stage. Survivors grow very slowly into a dense, rounded, rigidly branched grey shrub whose twigs end in spines and turn blackish when wet, hence the name.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Coleogyne ramosissima (slow-growing shrub 0.3-1.8 m on shallow soils, long-lived, flowers in spring from buds formed ~2 wk after March growth, apetalous solitary terminal flowers, wind-pollinated, achenes 3-4 mm, a masting species, rodent caches give clumped seedlings, 53-83% germination with 7 wk stratification, most seedlings die); ages estimated

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS Coleogyne ramosissima (solitary terminal flowers with 4 yellowish petal-like sepals and no petals, spring only; wind pollination; dry leathery achenes 3-4 mm with a twisted style, ripe early summer; mast years with huge crops, scatter-hoarded by rodents)

shrub.silhouette: broom of upright grey-green jointed stems

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two long, narrow, needle-like green cotyledons, then a thin jointed green stem with tiny paired scale leaves at the nodes. Grows slowly into a small tuft of stiff, erect, pale grey-green rush-like twigs; 5-10 years to reach knee height, then a dense broom-like mound. Seedlings are fragile; established plants resprout from the crown after fire or browsing.
growth.source: USDA FEIS species reviews (Ephedra nevadensis: 3-week prechill then germination at 20 C, 0.3-1.2 m tall, crown sprouting; Ephedra viridis: 0.6 m after 5-10 yr; Ephedra spp. surviving >100 yr in repeat-photo studies). First seed age estimated.

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS (Ephedra nevadensis: dioecious, wind-pollinated; cones form early spring, open Mar-May, seed mature early summer; seed cones 5-11 mm with 1-2 seeds 4-9 mm; large erratic crops; seeds cached by rodents). Colours, fruit set, hang, rot and crop estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling with two tiny cotyledons, then short, fleshy, cylindrical, needle-like leaves on a thin reddish stem above a deep taproot. The young plant becomes a few wiry, pale grey-brown, much-branched stems forming a low, tangled cushion-shrub; the small succulent leaves secrete salt and are shed in drought.
growth.source: Botanical knowledge, not confirmed online (Flora of China Tamaricaceae; Chinese ecophysiology studies of this Gobi xerohalophyte: fast germination after rain, salt-secreting leaves, drought deciduousness); growth and ages estimated

fruiting.source: Botanical knowledge, not confirmed online (Flora of China: small pink-white 5-petalled flowers, solitary or few at twig tips, Jul-Aug; small capsules splitting into 3-4 valves in Aug-Sep; seeds covered in long brown hairs, wind-dispersed); pollinators, set and crop estimated

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal seedling with two narrow, fleshy cotyledons, then narrow grey-green leaves coated in silvery scurf. On dry sites first-season seedlings may be only 3-4 cm tall while the taproot grows deep; young plants then branch from the base into a rounded, many-stemmed, silvery-grey shrub within 3-4 years.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Atriplex canescens (emergence 7-21 d after sowing, established in 3-4 yr, individuals survive 29 to over 100 yr); USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual, Atriplex (reproductive in the 2nd growing season, 21-day germination test).

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS (dioecious, wind-pollinated, fruits 0.8-1 cm with 4 papery wings, mature 3-4 months after flowering, semipersistent through winter); Woody Plant Seed Manual (17-120 thousand fruits/kg, crops 3 years in 5); seeds ground for meal by Native Americans; crop per plant estimated.

shrub.silhouette: gnarled grey tree with weeping leafless twigs

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds germinate within hours of wetting (the embryo is a ready-made, coiled green seedling) and emerge in 1-3 days: tiny green shoots with two slender cotyledons, then jointed, leafless green twigs. Deep roots race down; young plants are small feathery shrubs of drooping green twigs that later thicken into a gnarled, grey, twisted trunk.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Haloxylon ammodendron: 2-8 m, rarely 12 m; trunk to 25 cm); saxaul literature (very rapid germination, green spirally coiled embryo, short seed viability). Growth and ages estimated.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (tiny flowers Mar-Apr; fruit winged by the spreading perianth, ~8 mm across, pale brown or white wings, ripe Oct-Nov; seed 1.5 mm). Wind pollination, timings and counts estimated from shrubby Amaranthaceae.

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two narrow, woolly cotyledons, then narrow grey-green leaves thick with white star-shaped hairs. Seeds germinate even in near-freezing soil in early spring; the young plant is a small, woolly, silver-grey sprig with a deep taproot, branching from the base into a low, twiggy subshrub that turns white with fluffy fruits by autumn.
growth.source: USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual (Krascheninnikovia lanata, the North American winterfat: 20-80 cm, flowers Jun-Aug, wind-pollinated, hairy-bracted fruits dispersed fall-winter, may seed in the first year, germinates at near-freezing temperatures). Eurasian K. ceratoides is taller. Lifespan estimated.

fruiting.source: USDA WPSM (small grey-green wind-pollinated flowers Jun-Aug; one-seeded fruit in two bracts with tufts of white hairs 2-8 mm; disperses fall-winter; abundant annual crops). Timings, set and counts estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings emerge with the summer rains (June-July) as a thin tuft of narrow grey-green blades; roots reach about 25 cm in 6 weeks. From the second year scaly rhizomes 2.5-5 cm deep creep out (up to 1.5-1.8 m) and send up new tufts, so the plant becomes a patchy sod of stiff, curly-bladed culms 20-50 cm tall topped by compact spikes 3-7 cm long.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Pleuraphis jamesii (85% germination at 15.5-32 C; seedling roots 24.7 cm at 6 weeks; emergence June-July; rhizomes 1.5-1.8 m long, persist 5-7+ yr; resprouts regain preburn cover within 2 yr; culms 8-61 cm; spikes 3-7 cm). Age at first seed and plant lifespan estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: a single thread-thin, inrolled grey-green leaf after the awned grain drills into gravel; roots grow deep before the tuft thickens. Becomes a small, dense, grey-green tussock of wiry rolled leaves on stony desert steppe, its grains carrying long twisted awns that are feathery near the tip.
growth.source: Flora of China and Mongolian desert-steppe descriptions (short tussock 10-30 cm, awn plumose above); growth, flowering age and tussock lifespan estimated from Eurasian Stipa steppe grasses

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds are hard and often dormant for a year or more; seedlings appear mainly in cool, wet springs. The seedling is a single thin tiller with rolled, wiry, blue-green leaves above a fast, deep root; it slowly tillers into a small dense bunch and usually flowers from its second year, with airy, open panicles of plump black seeds on zigzag stalks.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Achnatherum hymenoides (seed dormancy, stratification in some ecotypes, 20 C optimum; seedling pulses follow wet Aprils; growth starts early Apr, seed ripe early Jul in Idaho; plants 10-61 cm tall, 20-30 cm across); first seed and lifespan estimated from bunchgrass habit
